SMTO-TSK-0048 — SMTO lost its place in the conversation list or history

GUID: 39a6a47c-8288-4257-8854-591dfe7cd3c1
Slug: conversation-cursor-stale
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't load the next part of a list or conversation because the marker it uses to remember where you were no longer matches. Your conversations themselves are not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page in your browser. Reloading throws away the old place marker and loads the list again from the top.
  2. If you were searching, clear the search box and type your search again instead of continuing to scroll the old results. A place marker from one search or filter doesn't work with a different one.
  3. Open the conversation again from the conversation list and scroll to the part you need. Opening it fresh gives SMTO a new, valid starting point for loading older messages.

What success looks like

  • The conversation list, search results or older messages load and you can keep scrolling.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the conversation to get past this; nothing in it was damaged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A conversation history, conversation index or search page request carried an invalid continuation cursor or boundary (malformed, from a different conversation or filter set, conflicting before/after/through/around selectors, or an out-of-range offset/limit).

What this means

  • History/search paging has a malformed cursor/boundary, mismatched filters, competing before/after/through/around selectors or invalid bounded offset/limit. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • History/search paging has a malformed cursor/boundary, mismatched filters, competing before/after/through/around selectors or invalid bounded offset/limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare cursor binding and current filters, and choose only one supported history boundary.

How to fix it

  • Discard the stored cursor and request the first page again with the current filters; cursors are scoped to one conversation and filter set and are not portable. For the Agent's history-reading tool, use an integer offset of 0 or more and a limit between 1 and 12000.
  • Refresh the conversation list or history window and start paging from the fresh response.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh bounded query returns a valid current continuation or history window.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
